stations.title: Benedictines near Burgos
stations.text: San Pedro de Cardeña arose as a Benedictine abbey near Burgos. Its foundation predates 902: on September 24, 902, Count Gonzalo Téllez and his wife Flámula gave the monastery land and salt pans as its first documented endowment. The start of building work is also given as 899.

stations.title: The Martyrs of Cardeña
stations.text: According to tradition, the monks were killed by Muslims in the 9th or 10th century; they were canonized in 1603 and venerated as the “Martyrs of Cardeña”. There is no documentary evidence for this.

stations.title: The Cid's monastery
stations.text: The Cid died in 1099 and was at first buried in Valencia. In 1102 his widow Jimena Díaz had the city evacuated, and his remains came to Cardeña. They stayed there for some years; the monastery remains closely associated with the Cid to this day.

stations.title: Suppression of the monasteries
stations.text: With the Desamortización under Mendizábal, Cardeña was suppressed and monastic life came to an end. The source consulted gives no exact year.

stations.title: A camp in the Civil War
stations.trigger_warning: Mentions the imprisonment and ill-treatment of prisoners of war.
stations.text: In the Spanish Civil War the empty monastery served as a concentration camp of the Francoist side for Republican prisoners of war, above all International Brigaders. It held more than 4,000 prisoners, including Basque soldiers and chaplains, and was closed in November 1939.

stations.title: Trappists return
stations.text: On May 1, 1942, monastic life was restored by Trappists from the monastery of San Isidro de Dueñas in the province of Palencia.

stations.title: Raised to an abbey
stations.text: In 1945 the community was raised to a priory and in 1948 to an abbey; its first abbot was Jesús Álvarez Álvarez. The monastery is near Castrillo del Val, east of Burgos.

stations.title: The first Spanish Trappist beer
stations.text: On March 16, 2016, Cardeña Tripel (7%) came onto the market, the first Spanish Trappist beer. It is brewed not in the monastery but at MarPal in Madrid and therefore does not bear the “Authentic Trappist Product” logo.

stations.title: Further beers
stations.text: According to Dutch Wikipedia, Cardeña Doble (6%) followed in 2021 and Cardeña Quadrupel (10%) in 2022. They too do not carry the ATP logo.
